TEAM PROJECT / NEST: A JOURNEY HOME

Help Terry find
a way home.

What we created

The README describes a simple 2D side-scrolling game inspired by classic Flash games. Players use the space bar to help Terry the Ant avoid roots and collect fruit to take home.

The repository includes C# scripts for movement and jumping, collectible interactions, score updates, menu actions, and scene reloads. Unity and Krita are the tools listed by the team.

View the original game-jam submission ↗

My participation

My résumé identifies this as a Unity and C# game-jam project, and the repository README credits Ximena M. alongside Allie H., Kenny V., Emma L., and Jesus G.

This is shared team work. The public files reviewed do not establish my individual script ownership. The skills below describe learning opportunities and technical concepts demonstrated by the project; the exact division of work and personal learning outcomes still need my confirmation.

02 / SKILLS & LEARNING

What building this
project helps me practice.

These reflections connect visible code to transferable skills, without claiming sole authorship.

01 / PROGRAMMING

C# and component-based logic

Working with Unity scripts introduces classes, fields, methods, enums, lists, and components. Movement.cs connects player input, speed settings, and a Rigidbody2D.

Learning focus: Break an interactive feature into manageable behaviors and state.

02 / INTERACTION

Input, movement & physics

Movement code uses frame time, jump velocity, gravity adjustments, and a ground check. The project illustrates how input becomes a visible response.

Learning focus: Reason about timing, conditions, and how a system responds to a user.

03 / STATE & FEEDBACK

Events, collections & UI

Trigger callbacks detect collectible interactions. The score script increments a number and updates TextMeshPro text; movement code also tracks collected item types in a list.

Learning focus: Connect events to state changes and clear feedback.

Team development

The README identifies a five-person first-time game-development team. A shared project provides practice coordinating features and integrating code with visual assets. My broader résumé also lists GitHub collaboration.

Reflection to confirm: Which feature did I own, how did we divide tasks, and what did I change after testing?

Iteration and debugging

The scripts provide useful material for explaining edge cases, such as jump conditions, collision behavior, and score updates. A future case-study update can document an actual bug, its fix, and a repeatable check.

Next evidence: Add my contribution notes, one before/after example, and a short gameplay recording.

04 / CONNECTION TO MY CAREER

From interactive games
to useful AI experiences.

This project gives me an early example of software that responds to users through rules, state, and feedback. Those concepts can support future work on interfaces and integrations for AI applications.

My next step is to add Python APIs, data handling, evaluation, and deployment through a separate AI project. Nest is a game-development project; it does not demonstrate model training or production AI experience.
